title: What Lester liked to hear in 1933: Teagarden's break on Dinah
summary: Lester listened little but liked Jack Teagarden's riff on Red Nichols's Dinah; Phillips describes how Teagarden changed the trombone.

bands.name: Red Nichols and His Five Pennies

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: This was in '33, when Prez was in the band.
Yeah.
What records...? Was he into listening a lot at that time or was he into just playing? What was doing at that time in terms of listening?
He never listened too much.
at that point?
Yeah. He never did too much listening. He'd hear some things, and say "That sounds all right" -- you know, like that. But I mean, he...
What, for example, did he say sounded all right at that point?
Something somebody made. Some kind of pass a cat made on a horn.
Phillips - 140
Anything you might remember in particular?
He used to like this riff Jack Teagarden used to make on "Dinah."
What record of "Dinah" was that?
The one he made with Red Nichols. Did you ever hear that?
I think I heard that. Maybe Babe Russin might have been on it -- tenor player.
No, there wasn't no tenor on this one.
Well, he might have been playing baritone or something.
No, this one had nothing but a clarinet -- I think Benny Goodman playing clarinet -- and Red on trumpet, and Jack Teagarden on trombone, Eddie Lang playing guitar...
This was back in the 20's then.
Yeah. And Rollini was playin' that bass sax.
Adrian Rollini.
Adrian, yeah. He was playing that sax. Didn't have but three horns on it.
What did he used to say about it?

He used to like the riff Jack Teagarden did. He said... [SINGS] Les said, 'That's pretty.' He liked that. But anybody would, to hear him play that in them days. Because see, he changed trombone around. Cats be saying, YAH-YAH-YAH-YAH-YAHHH/YAAAAHH... He'd come in, 'DA-RA-BE-DA-RA-BE-
Phillips - 141

DU-DA/RAB-BAH-DEE-TE-DERRM-DA-DA/BO-BU." Then he used to play [SINGS] -- playing trombone fast. That break he made: "BEEP/BREEP/BA-BU-DE-DU...[ETC.]" He played the break in there for about 4 bars. And we used to listen to that. Of course, we used to listen to everything practically Red Nichols played and Bix. See, they was guys out there who was playing Jazz then.
Talk about that.
Well, in a big band, you couldn't get no...
Well, the Goldkette band and the Henderson band...
Yeah, Goldkette... Well, after Bix left him and went to Whiteman... Anyway, those are the tunes that he used to like to hear.
We talked about that earlier, but that's interesting.
Yeah.
